column3: It nearly repeats the focus: on that Day the wrongdoers' excuses do not benefit and no redress is granted.
God's curse and an evil destination closely match the focus's paired consequences for wrongdoers.
It confirms the comprehensive divine and communal curse, but does not add the futile-excuse or abode setting.
The Day when wealth and children do not benefit gives a close general counterpart to the focus's failed excuse.
It identifies Pharaoh's people's wrongful earthly exultation as an antecedent to the nearby condemnation.
The curse following Aad in this world and on the Resurrection Day closely extends the focus's enduring exclusion.
The curse lasting until the Day of Judgment supplies the temporal horizon of the focus's curse.
The invoked curse on liars is a limited procedural parallel, without the focus's final judgment scene.
Calling an alleged offender a wrongdoer shares only the designation, not the Day, excuse, or consequence.
On the Day of Decision, late faith does not benefit disbelievers, closely paralleling the focus's closed opportunity.
The immediately preceding Day of witnesses supplies the evidentiary setting in which excuses lose force.
Successive communities enter the Fire together and curse one another, extending the focus's exclusion into a judgment scene.
It joins curse and an evil abode for covenant-breakers, directly matching the focus's final pair of consequences.
Curse, divine anger, Hell, and great punishment give a closely aligned outcome for deliberate wrongdoing.
Its worldly inheritance discussion of relative benefit does not clarify the final futility of excuses.
Wrongdoers face the evil punishment on the Resurrection Day, supplying the punitive horizon behind the focus.
The subsequent gift of guidance and Scripture gives only broad local contrast to the condemned wrongdoers.
Its Day of exact recompense and absence of injustice supports the justice of the focus's irreversible verdict.
The denial of divine wrongdoing and attribution of wrongdoing to them directly supports the focus's culpability premise.
A curse in this world and on the Resurrection Day provides another close model of sustained exclusion.
The brief pairing of excuse and warning does not explain why excuses fail at final judgment.
Divine curse, lasting Hell, and permanent punishment closely reinforce the focus's terminal condemnation.
The statement about the Book's revelation does not add to excuses, curse, or final abode.
A curse continuing to the Day of Judgment supplies a related temporal and punitive frame.
On the Resurrection Day, covenant-breakers receive no divine address or purification and face painful punishment.
The nearby Fire dispute supplies the immediate social setting for the focus's judgment against wrongdoers.
Recompense by what each soul earned, without injustice, grounds the focus's denial that excuses can reverse judgment.
Lack of guidance and painful punishment for unbelief offers only a general outcome parallel.
Its cursed tree and warning concern a distinct sign and do not develop the focus's final exclusion.
Divine anger, curse, Hell, and an evil destination form a close composite parallel to the focus.
Witnesses identify liars before their Lord and proclaim God's curse upon wrongdoers, closely linking proof and curse.
The same-surah rule of proportionate repayment for evil acts explains why post hoc excuses cannot alter the result.
On the Resurrection Day false allies reject and curse one another before the Fire, closely extending the focus's outcome.
The refusal of permission to offer excuses directly clarifies the focus's claim that excuses no longer avail.
A curse in this world and disgrace on the Resurrection Day closely parallels the focus's lasting exclusion.
The reminder benefiting believers provides only a broad contrary use of benefit.
The declaration that wrongdoers do not prosper and the final abode becomes known supplies a related outcome frame.
God's judgment by truth in the same surah directly grounds the focus's decisive judgment against wrongdoers.
Benefit from remembrance concerns receptive guidance, only distantly contrasting with the focus's failed excuse.
Severe punishment lasting to the Resurrection Day gives a related enduring-consequence frame.
Expulsion from divine presence is a compact counterpart to the exclusion named by the focus's curse.
Curse for disobedience and transgression supplies a clear wrongdoing-to-exclusion relation.
The command not to make excuses today directly restates the focus's final futility of excuses.
Prideful refusal of worship leads to entering Hell humbled, giving immediate-surah cause and destination.
Worldly benefits and drinks do not clarify final judgment or the failure of excuses.
The Day when truthfulness benefits the truthful gives a precise positive contrast to wrongdoers' useless excuses.
Entry through Hell's gates and its evil lodging for the arrogant closely supplies the focus's evil abode.
The absence of blame on one who seeks redress after being wronged concerns a different legal setting.
The final abode and the failure of wrongdoers offer a concise parallel to the focus's evil destination.
The exception for divine mercy does not itself clarify the focus's grounds for curse or futile excuses.
Divine curse caused by disbelief gives a direct but partial counterpart to the focus's curse.
God's lack of love for wrongdoers is a general moral contrast without the focus's judgment sequence.
The Fire keepers reject a condemned group's plea, closely reinforcing the ineffectiveness of late appeals nearby.
Once the promise proves true, God's curse upon wrongdoers is publicly announced in a final-reckoning scene.
The remembrance of the abode for chosen servants does not clarify the wrongdoers' evil abode.
The creative command does not add to final accountability, excuse, or curse.
Objects unable to harm or benefit offer a remote contrast to the focus's claim that an excuse cannot benefit.
A curse in this world and the Hereafter with great punishment closely supports the focus's enduring exclusion.
Moses's mission with signs supplies background to Pharaoh's narrative but not the focus's judgment claim itself.
Permission to defend those wronged is a worldly contrast, not an account of wrongdoers' final fate.
Even all earthly wealth cannot ransom wrongdoers from the evil punishment on the Resurrection Day.
Clear proofs were rejected before divine seizure, supplying immediate-surah culpability for the focus's verdict.
Those who conceal clear guidance are cursed by God and by those who curse, giving a partial consequence parallel.
The prayer not to be made a trial for wrongdoers does not clarify their final excuse or curse.
Pilgrimage benefits and provision do not illuminate the focus's final judgment.
What benefits people remaining in the earth is only a broad conceptual contrast to an excuse that does not benefit.
The limit on retribution and God's dislike of wrongdoers provides only a general justice principle.
The stages of human creation do not add to the Day, excuse, curse, or abode.
The inability of false objects to benefit or harm is a remote counterpart to failed reliance.
The good final abode for the patient supplies a clear contrary destination to the focus's evil abode.
The miserly exercise of imagined political share does not clarify final accountability.
No compensation, intercession, or help benefits on that Day, broadly paralleling the focus's failed excuse.
When decisive signs arrive, newly professed faith does not benefit, closely clarifying the closure described in the focus.
The account of Abraham's family and favor does not illuminate the focus's judgment scene.
Those who die in disbelief bear God's, angels', and all people's curse, closely matching enduring exclusion.
The Day when every deed is presented and evil is wished far away supports the exposure behind failed excuses.
The question whether idols benefit or harm gives only a general test of reliance.
A person remains aware of himself even while presenting excuses, directly explaining why excuses cannot overturn the verdict.
God curses disbelievers and prepares a blazing Fire, closely pairing exclusion with final destination.
In the same surah, wrongdoers have no close friend or obeyed intercessor on the impending Day.
The worldly balance of benefit and harm in intoxicants and gambling does not clarify final excuses.
A leader brings his people to the Fire on the Resurrection Day, with an evil destination, closely extending wrongdoers' end.
God's curse is joined to deafness and blindness, showing exclusion's disabling consequence.
Wrongdoers are deferred only to a terrifying Day, directly framing the delayed judgment in which excuses fail.
Learning what harms rather than benefits and losing the Hereafter gives a partial, non-judgmental consequence parallel.
Past communities' embellished deeds and painful punishment supply only broad antecedent context.
Those accursed are exposed to seizure and killing, a forceful but worldly form of exclusion.
Multiplied punishment on the Resurrection Day and enduring humiliation reinforce the focus's terminal consequence.
On that Day, having wronged themselves, sharing punishment will not benefit them, an especially close verbal and thematic parallel.
Leaders who call to the Fire receive no help on the Resurrection Day, closely countering any hope of rescue.
Rejected signs and the meeting with God lead to worthless deeds and no weight on the Resurrection Day.
The Day when people stand before the Lord supplies the formal judgment setting for the focus.
Preferring worldly life and refusal of guidance gives a broad antecedent to the focus's final condemnation.
The promised consequence appearing as brief and the destruction of the defiantly disobedient give a related final-warning frame.
The oath by the promised Day names the setting but adds no specific account of excuses or punishment.
Contentment with worldly life and heedlessness of signs supplies only general antecedent context.
The Day when secrets are tested explains why concealed responsibility cannot be covered by an excuse.
Its fasting and marital regulations do not clarify the focus's final judgment.
Inheritance shares and the rule against harm do not clarify the focus's final judgment.
Nursing, maintenance, and family obligations do not add to excuses, curse, or evil abode.
Angels reject the claimed helplessness of wrongdoers and assign them Hell as an evil destination, making this a direct missing parallel.
God curses those who choose false authorities, and the cursed find no helper.
Those who disbelieve and commit wrongdoing are neither forgiven nor guided, establishing a closely related final exclusion.
The wrongdoers' only stated path is Hell, where they remain, directly supplying the focus's evil abode.
Those who ascribe partners are barred from the Garden and enter the Fire, with no helpers for wrongdoers.
Those who deny the signs and act arrogantly are companions of the Fire, supplying the terminal outcome of rejection.
People of the Fire plead for water and provision but are refused, a close scene of futile post-judgment appeal.
When the realization arrives, those who neglected it acknowledge their loss after the time for remedy has passed.
Evil deeds receive like recompense, faces are covered in humiliation, and their destination is the Fire.
The destruction of past peoples is explicitly not divine wrongdoing but the result of their own wrongdoing.
Wrongdoers could offer all the earth and more as ransom, yet face an evil reckoning and Hell as their abode.
Hell, foul drink, and an inescapable death frame a closely related evil destination.
Weak followers and arrogant leaders stand before God; the leaders admit they cannot help, directly clarifying failed dependence at judgment.
Satan disowns those who followed him and denies having power over them, sharply exposing the failure of excuses based on misleading allegiance.
Those who mislead others bear their own burdens and part of others' burdens on the Resurrection Day.
On the Resurrection Day God disgraces those who associated partners and exposes their false claims.
When a witness is raised from every community, wrongdoers receive neither permission to speak nor an opening for appeasement.
Once wrongdoers see the punishment, it is neither lightened nor delayed.
Those gathered blind, mute, and deaf have Hell as their refuge, and its blaze is increased.
Those who called alleged partners find that they do not answer and that no escape exists between them.
The criminals see the Fire, become certain they will fall into it, and find no way to turn aside.
Faces submit to the Ever-Living Sustainer, and one carrying wrongdoing has failed.
Turning away from remembrance leads to constricted life and blind Resurrection, a related consequence of rejected guidance.
Those whose scales are light lose themselves and remain in Hell.
The condemned confess that wretchedness overcame them and plead for removal from the Fire, a direct model of belated appeal.
The command to remain in the Fire without speaking establishes the closure of such post-judgment pleading.
The condemned wish for a return so that they could become believers, directly showing the irreversibility of the final state.
Those who bring evil are cast face-first into the Fire and repaid only for what they did.
Those summoned to call their alleged partners receive no answer and see the punishment, exposing false reliance at judgment.
A witness is brought from every community and proof is demanded, supplying the evidentiary setting in which excuses fail.
Hell encompasses the disbelievers, closely reinforcing the focus's evil abode.
When the Hour rises, the criminals fall into despair.
The associators have no intercessors among their alleged partners and disown those partners at judgment.
On the Day no parent can avail a child and no child can avail a parent, a broad counterpart to the focus's failed excuse.
On that Day none can benefit or harm another, and wrongdoers are directed to the punishment they denied.
Those who disbelieve remain in Hell; neither death nor reduction of punishment is granted.
The inhabitants of Hell plead for another chance to act rightly and are answered that their allotted warning-time has passed.
Those who led and followed in error share the punishment together, closely extending collective culpability after judgment.
The soul's lament over neglecting God is an explicit late regret that cannot undo the outcome.
The claim that guidance would have produced piety is a direct form of the too-late excuse addressed by the focus.
The wish for one more return to become righteous directly parallels the focus's closed remedial opportunity.
The reply that signs came and were denied establishes why the later excuse is ineffective.
The disbelievers are driven to Hell after messengers' warnings are recalled, directly joining prior proof to final confinement.
Hell is named the evil abode of the arrogant, an exact counterpart to the focus's evil abode.
All parties in the Fire are told that God has judged among the servants, immediately extending the focus's final verdict.
The Fire's inhabitants ask its keepers for a reduction of punishment, a nearby instance of futile appeal.
The Fire is their abode if they endure, and even seeking appeasement does not make them among those admitted to it.
The criminals remain in punishment without relief, reinforcing the permanence of the focus's consequence.
The condemned appeal to the keeper of Hell for an end, but are told they will remain.
God's dominion over the heavens and earth culminates in the Day when the Hour arrives and falsifiers lose.
Those who mocked God's signs and were deceived by worldly life enter the Fire with no exit or appeasement.
On the Day of presentation to the Fire, arrogant disbelievers are assigned humiliating punishment for their conduct.
At judgment, accusation and dispute are closed: the divine word does not change and no injustice is done to servants.
Scheming does not benefit wrongdoers on the Day when they are struck down, a close counterpart to futile excuse.
The criminals are dragged into the Fire and told to taste its touch, supplying the realized punishment.
Hypocrites ask believers for light but are separated by a wall, a related image of irreversible exclusion.
Wealth and children do not avail their owners against God, adding a broad analogue to the focus's useless excuse.
Satan disowns the person he led into disbelief, clarifying the collapse of a misleading alliance at final consequence.
Seeking forgiveness or not seeking it makes no difference for persistent hypocrites, a related closure of intercession.
Those who disbelieve receive Hell, described as an evil destination.
The inhabitants of the Blaze acknowledge that hearing or reasoning would have prevented their fate, a direct self-indictment after the fact.
The command to seize and burn the condemned person gives the executed form of final punishment.
The food of the condemned is restricted to the sinful, sealing the social and punitive exclusion.
No devoted friend asks after another on the Day, even though each is shown the other, directly negating hoped-for rescue.
The criminal wishes to ransom himself with family and all on earth, an especially close analogue to a futile excuse or substitute.
The people of the right ask the criminals what brought them into the Fire, opening an explicit account of culpability.
No intercession benefits the criminals, directly paralleling the focus's statement that an excuse does not benefit.
The wrongdoer, confronted with what his hands sent ahead, wishes he had been dust.
On the Day a person remembers what he strove for, supplying the exposure of deeds behind the focus's failed defense.
Criminals are veiled from their Lord on that Day, a close form of the focus's curse as exclusion.
After that exclusion, the criminals enter the Blaze.
Faces are humbled on that Day, supplying a concise contrast to worldly arrogance.
Those humbled faces enter a scorching Fire.
